description: Defines the five Book 5 (TEL) operators, their roles, invariant bindings, phase assignments, and sequence within the TEL evaluation cycle.

operators.name: SyntaxCheck
operators.role: Validates a TEL expression against the canonical grammar defined in tel.syntax_map. Returns PASS or FAIL with a structured parse report.
operators.output: parse_result ∈ {pass, fail}; if pass: parse_tree; if fail: error_report with grammar rule violated
preconditions: Raw expression E is provided as a string or token stream
postconditions: If PASS: parse_tree is available for TEL-Ε. If FAIL: evaluation halts; expression must be corrected.
must_not: Infer meaning from an ill-formed expression
Attempt partial evaluation of a failed parse
Accept an expression that violates WF-001 through WF-006
operators.notes: First operator in every TEL evaluation session. No other operator may execute before TEL-Σ returns PASS. A failed TEL-Σ is not a semantic judgment — it is a grammar rejection.

operators.name: Evaluate
operators.role: Applies canonical evaluation rules (tel.semantics_map) to the parse_tree produced by TEL-Σ. Produces a structural denotation for the input expression.
operators.input: parse_tree from TEL-Σ (PASS), active module registry, current evaluation scope
operators.output: structural_denotation S or evaluation_fault ∈ {EF-001, EF-002, EF-003, EF-004, EF-005}
postconditions: Each sub-expression has a recorded structural denotation
All faults are recorded in the session fault log
Scope is updated with any T[…] or C[…] declarations
must_not: Proceed on a FAIL parse_tree from TEL-Σ
Assign multiple interpretations to a single expression
Substitute a default value for an UnresolvedIdentifier (EF-001)
operators.notes: Core semantic engine of TEL. INV-TEL-002 (Semantic Stability) is the governing invariant: one expression, one denotation. Any session that produces ambiguous denotations has an implementation bug, not a valid semantic result.
operators.book4_binding: OR operator denotations are resolved via Book 4 module when active

operators.name: Compose
operators.role: Assembles compound TEL expressions from evaluated sub-expressions according to composition rules in tel.composition_map. Ensures INV-TEL-003 (Compositionality) is satisfied at every composition site.
operators.input: Two or more structural denotations from TEL-Ε, applicable compose_op, composition context
preconditions: All sub-expressions to be composed have been evaluated by TEL-Ε
No unresolved EF-001 or EF-002 faults in sub-expression results
postconditions: Composition ordering rules (COR-001 through COR-004) have been verified
No holistic meaning has been introduced beyond sub-expression contributions
must_not: Introduce implicit context not encoded in sub-expressions or composition rules
Apply operator precedence not grounded in parenthetical grouping
Compose across books without verifying active module registry contains all required books
operators.notes: TEL-Κ is not a standalone operator in the sense that composition is always driven by TEL-Ε at the compound expression nodes of the parse_tree. TEL-Κ is the designated auditor that verifies INV-TEL-003 compliance at each composition step.

operators.name: Transform
operators.role: Encodes and applies named structural transformations declared in TEL expressions (T[ID] blocks). Verifies INV-TEL-004 (Transformation Fidelity) at each application site.
operators.input: Transformation declaration T[ID] with input expression e_in and output expression e_out; target structure S to transform
preconditions: T[ID] has been declared and evaluated in current scope
Target structure S is structurally valid (validated against Book 1 kernel constraints)
T[ID] is applicable to S — its input type matches S's structural type
postconditions: If S' is structurally valid: transformation recorded as PASS
If S' is structurally invalid: EF-005 recorded; T[ID] declaration flagged for revision

gate_logic.fidelity_fail: valid(S) ∧ applicable(T, S) ∧ ¬valid(S') → record EF-005, halt T[ID] application

must_not: Apply a transformation to a structurally invalid input and report the output as valid
Suppress EF-005 and deliver S' without the fault record
Modify ω(S) as a side-effect of transformation without an explicit OR-Ω re-evaluation in the active session

downstream_bindings.book6_governance: Regime constraint enforcement transformations use TEL-Τ to encode constraint-change operators
downstream_bindings.book7_sarg: SARG argument structure transformations (warrant addition, claim substitution) are encoded as TEL-Τ expressions
downstream_bindings.book8_nos: Identity-through-change analysis (INV-NOS-003) uses TEL-Τ to express structure-preserving and identity-breaking transformations
downstream_bindings.book9_pattern_dynamics: Pattern mutation and bifurcation events are modelled as TEL-Τ sequences

operators.notes: TEL-Τ is the primary mechanism by which the AI Edition represents structural change in a machine-readable form. All transformation claims in downstream books must have a corresponding TEL-Τ encoding to be formally valid.

operators.name: Assert
operators.role: Evaluates invariant assertion expressions (INV[ID]: assert e) and constraint assertion sites (e1 ⊢ e2). Records PASS or InvariantViolation / ConstraintViolation (EF-003, EF-004).
operators.input: Invariant ID from active book's invariants file, structural denotation of asserted expression e
preconditions: Referenced invariant ID exists in the active book's invariants file
Asserted expression e has been evaluated by TEL-Ε without EF-001 or EF-002 faults
postconditions: Assertion result recorded in session audit log
All InvariantViolation results are propagated to downstream session consumers
Session is not silently clean if any assertion fails
must_not: Accept a forward reference to an undeclared invariant ID
Suppress an InvariantViolation and report PASS
Evaluate nested INV[…] inside T[…] or C[…] blocks — this is a grammar violation
operators.notes: TEL-Α is the final gatekeeper of the evaluation cycle. It ensures that completed TEL encodings respect the declared invariants of the active books. It is the only operator that directly surfaces InvariantViolation results to the session consumer.
